questions.question:
Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given.

There were more than thirty delegates who attend the training programme last summer.

options.text: There are more than thirty delegates who attend the training programme last summer
There were more than thirty delegates who attends the training programme last summer.
There was more than thirty delegates who attend the training programme last summer
There were more than thirty delegates who attended the training programme last summer.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is, '**There were more than thirty delegates who attended the training programme last summer.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Since the training programme happened last year, all the details of that time will be in the Past Tense.
 
• There **were** more than thirty delegates who **attended** the training programme last summer.
 
 
• Past tense of 'to be verb' will be plural because it is talking about the plural common noun, 'thirty delegates'.
 
• The event took place in the past and any reference to that event will also be in the past, using the Past Tense.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There **are** more than thirty delegates who** attend** the training programme last summer.

 
 
• As the event took place in the past, verbs should also be in the Past Tense.
 
 
 
• There were more than thirty delegates who **attends** the training programme last summer.
 
 
• Simple form of any verb with s (makes) or es (does) is used for third-person-singular in the Present Simple Tense.
 
• Example, ***Joey cooks delicious pasta.***
 
 
 
• There **was** more than thirty delegates who **attend** the training programme last summer.
 
 
• For common nouns in plural we use the plural form of 'to be verb' - were and are.
 
• The event took place in the past, so the Past Tense should be used.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The teacher gave the question paper.

options.text: The question paper was given by the teacher.
The question paper was being given by the teacher.
The question paper was gave by the teacher.
The question paper has been given by the teacher.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is, '**The question paper was given by the teacher**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active and Passive rules say that every Active sentence is turned into a Passive voice by making the doer of Active which is the subject, then the object of the Passive sentence.
 
 
• Example, Active Voice - ***Leah baked the cake.*** Here Leah is the doer and subject of this sentence.

 
 
• Passive Voice - ***The cake was baked by Leah***. Leah is still the doer, but now is the subject of the sentence.
 
 
 
 
 
• Active and Passive rules also state that a sentence of Past Simple Tense use 'was/were + verb' when changed from Active to Passive Voice.
 
 
• Example, Active Voice - ***Jake completed the work.***
 
 
• Passive Voice, ***The work was completed by Jake.***
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The following are the Changes in Tense from Active to Passive, for the Past Tense sentences:
 
 
• Past Simple Tense (2nd form of the verb → was/were + 3rd form of the verb)
 
 
• Example, Active Voice - ***Ria dropped the keys.*** Passive Voice - ***The keys were dropped by Ria.***
 
 
 
• Past Continuous ( was + ing-verb → was being + 3rd form of the verb)
 
 
• ​Example, ***Harry was painting the picture***. Passive Voice - ***The picture was being painted by Harry.***
 
 
 
 
 
• The following table provides the active and passive forms of verbs.

__
 
• **Revenue Receipts**

 
 
• **Revenue receipts** are defined as **those receipts that neither increase a government's liabilities nor decrease its assets**.
 
• They are **routine and ongoing in nature**, and the government receives them as **part of daily operations**.
 
• **Taxes and other levies collected by the Centre, interest and dividends received on investments, and fees and charges paid to the government for services** are all considered revenue receipts.
 
• Revenue receipts must meet the** following two requirements**:
 
 
• **No liability:** The** government is not liable for any revenue received**. For example, unlike borrowings, taxes received by the government do not result in any liabilities for it.
 
• **No asset reduction: **The **amount of assets owned by the government does not decrease as a result of revenue**. Therefore, because the sale of the share reduced the government's assets, it is not possible for it to report the earnings from the sale of the stake as revenue.

• **Capital Receipts**

 
 
• **Receipts that create liabilities or decrease financial assets are referred to as capital receipts**.
 
• **Incoming monetary flows** are also referred as Capital receipts. 
 
• Both **debt and non-debt capital receipts** are possible.
 
• Capital receipts are significantly **influenced by loans from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), foreign governments, and the general public**.
 
• The** government's estimated capital receipts for the 2020–21 financial year were Rs. 1,074,306 crore**.
 
• While the **actual capital receipts for the 2018–19 Budget were Rs 763,518 crore**, the **revised **projections for the **2019–20 Budget came in at Rs 772,529 crore**.

questions.question: With reference to the major regions of the northern plains, Bhabar is:

options.text: the older alluvium along the river beds forming terraces higher than the flood plain
a narrow belt of about 8 to 16 km that runs in the west-east direction along the foot of the Himalayas from the river Indus to Teesta
composed of newer alluvium and forms flood plains along the river banks
a broad long zone of northern India and southern Nepal running parallel to the lower ranges of the Himalayas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **After going down **from the **mountain **a **narrow belt **is formed which **is 8-16 km by the deposition **of **river pebbles**. This **belt **is called **Bhabar**. 
 
• It lies **parallel **to the **Shiwalik range**. **Streams again appear **in this **region **and **make it a wet **and **marshy region**.
 
• **The bhabar **tract comprises gravel and **un-assorted sediment deposits**.
 
• **This sediment present **in the **soil **is **deposited **by **rivers descending **from the **Himalayan mountains**.
 
• **This region **is not **good for cultivation**. **The area **is popular **with big trees with large roots**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhangar** - is the older alluvium along the river beds forming terraces, which are dark in colour, rich in humus content and productive. Bhangar is generally a well-drained and the most productive land of the Great Plains of India.
 
• **The Khadar** is composed of newer alluvium and forms the flood plains along the river banks. They are sandy clays and loams, drier and leached, less calcareous and carbonaceous.
 
• **Tarai,** also spelled Terai, region of northern India and southern Nepal running parallel to the lower ranges of the Himalayas.

questions.question: Areas like the southern part of Gujarat, eastern Tamil Nadu, northeast peninsula covering Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, and East Madhya Pradesh receive rainfall between _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100-200 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rainfall between 100-200 **cm is **received **in the **southern parts of Gujarat**, **east Tamil Nadu**, **northeastern Peninsula covering Odisha**, **Jharkhand**, **Bihar**, **eastern Madhya Pradesh**, **northern Ganga **plain along the **sub-Himalayas **and the **Cachar Valley **and **Manipur**.
 
• They are the **area of Medium Rainfall**.
 
• **Duration of the monsoon in India**-
 
 
• The **Southern part of India**, being **near to the sea**, **gets rainfall early **and **for a longer duration **than the **northern part**.
 
• **As rain-bearing winds cross western ghats **humidity **decreases **and so **does rainfall in the northern part of India**.
 
• The **Southern part **of India **receives rainfall from the southwest monsoon **and the retreating **southwest monsoon **(**northeast monsoon**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The monsoon rainfall **has a **declining **trend with **increasing distance **from the **sea**. **Kolkata receives 119 cm **during **the southwest monsoon period, Patna 105 cm**, **Allahabad 76 cm**, and **Delhi 56 cm**.
 
• The **highest rainfall **occurs along **the west coast**, on **the Western Ghats**, as well as in the **sub-Himalayan areas **in the **northeast **and the **hills of Meghalaya**. Here the **rainfall exceeds 200 cm**. In **some parts **of **Khasi and Jaintia hills**, the **rainfall exceeds 1,000 cm**. They are the **area of high Rainfall**.
 
• **Western Uttar Pradesh**, **Delhi**, **Haryana**, **Punjab**, **Jammu **and **Kashmir**, **eastern Rajasthan**, **Gujarat**, and **Deccan Plateau **receives **rainfall between 50-100 cm**. They are the **area of Low Rainfall**.
 
• **Parts of the Peninsula**, especially in **Andhra Pradesh**, **Karnataka and Maharashtra**, **Ladakh**, and **most of western Rajasthan receive rainfall below 50 cm**. It is the **area of Inadequate Rainfall**.

questions.question: In which of the following years was India the host of the Asian Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951 and 1982**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Asian Games**, also known as **Asiad**, is **a continental multi-sport **event held **every four years **among **athletes **from **all over Asia**.
 
• The **Games **were **regulated **by the **Asian Games Federation **from **the first Games in New Delhi**, **India**, **until **the **1978 Games**.
 
• It was **firstly organized **in the **1951 Asian Games in New Delhi, India**.
 
• **New Delhi**, the national **capital of India**, has **hosted the Asian Games **on **two occasions**: **the inaugural 1951 Asian Games **and the **1982 Asian Games**.
 
• Asian Games, 2023 will be a multi-sport event celebrated in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There have been **nine nations that have hosted **the Asian Games. Forty-six nations have participated in the Games, including Israel, which was excluded from the Games altogether after Israel managed to win a silver medal (in their last participation) at the 1974 Asian Games in Iran. The most recent games were held in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia from 18 August to 2 September 2018.
 
• The Asian Games Movement uses symbols to represent the** ideals embodied in the Asian Games charter.**
